en.title: David Fincher's American Squid Game Spinoff Reportedly Shelved by Netflix
en.summary: The highly anticipated English-language adaptation of the global phenomenon Squid Game, helmed by director David Fincher, appears to be no longer moving forward at Netflix. This decision marks a significant shift in the streamer's strategy for the popular franchise.
en.body:
The dream of a David Fincher-directed American take on **Squid Game** has reportedly been dashed. For years, whispers and reports have suggested the acclaimed filmmaker was developing an English-language spinoff of the South Korean survival thriller, even working under the working title *Heckler*. However, recent sources close to the project indicate that Netflix has decided to shelve the ambitious adaptation, signaling a potential pivot in the streamer's approach to the **Squid Game** universe.

This news comes after a protracted development period. Back in 2024, reports surfaced that Fincher had been quietly working on the project for some time, with British writer Dennis Kelly attached. The possibility of such a high-profile adaptation gained further traction with the surprising appearance of Cate Blanchett in the final moments of the original **Squid Game** series, a move many interpreted as a direct tease for an American expansion. Despite these indicators and even a listing on the Film and Television Industry Alliance website in late 2025 suggesting a February 2026 shoot in Los Angeles under the title *Squid Game: America*, the project seems to have hit a definitive dead end.

## A Shift in Streaming Priorities

The reasons behind Netflix's reported decision appear to stem from evolving internal priorities and Fincher's own packed schedule. Sources suggest that after years of development and executive changes within the streamer, Netflix's focus for the **Squid Game** franchise has shifted. This, coupled with Fincher's commitments to other projects, including the reportedly baffling sequel to *Once Upon a Time in Hollywood*, **The Adventures of Cliff Booth**, has likely contributed to the shelving of *Heckler*. It’s a familiar story in the streaming landscape: projects can languish for years, only to be re-evaluated or canceled as platform strategies morph.

## What This Means for Fans

For the legions of **Squid Game** fans worldwide, this news is undoubtedly a disappointment. The prospect of Fincher, known for his meticulous direction and dark, atmospheric thrillers like **Se7en** and **Zodiac**, bringing his signature style to the brutal world of deadly children's games was a tantalizing one. The original series, created by **Hwang Dong-hyuk**, became a global cultural phenomenon, and the idea of a Western counterpart helmed by a director of Fincher's caliber generated significant excitement. While the Korean original remains a benchmark, many were eager to see how Fincher would interpret its themes and aesthetics for an international audience.

## What's Next

While David Fincher's **Squid Game** adaptation may not be moving forward, Netflix has confirmed that a reality competition series based on the show, **Squid Game: The Challenge**, is slated for release in November 2024. Further details regarding any other potential expansions or continuations of the **Squid Game** universe have not yet been announced.
